title: Fun in the Wind
checkpoint: Reception Summer 1, week 2 — Phase 4: CCVC words: two consonant sounds together at the start (no new sounds)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 4 book full of blends at the start and end of words, like strong, gust and shed. If a word feels long, split it into two chunks and blend the chunks together.

pages.illustration: The whole garden bending in a gale — trees on the diagonal, leaves streaming off the page, washing horizontal on the line. No characters yet. Set the force up.
Pip clamped to a branch with both feet and both wings, tail blown straight out sideways, eyes squeezed shut. Very funny.
Nell blown clean off her flight path, tumbling sideways with her legs waving, drawn as a small yellow blur.
A large twig snapping off the oak and falling across the frame, leaves streaming. Both characters diving clear below it.
Pip and Nell scrambling low across the grass together, using the ground for shelter, grass flattened all round them.
The garden shed appearing through the wind, its door swinging, warm dark safety inside. The pair heading for it.

pages.text: It was snug in the shed.
pages.illustration: Interior of the shed: cosy clutter of flowerpots and string, both of them tucked between the pots, wind howling past the window.

pages.text: The wind did stop at last.
pages.illustration: Closing page: the door open on a completely still garden, everything upright again, one leaf falling gently. The pair stepping out. Calm after storm.
